# prefill expert cost at higher quant: does the 5.70 us/expert-bucket primitive (D18, measured at K=3)
# hold at K=4/K=6, or does it scale with bytes? 2.05 arm for comparison is out_prefill_scale.txt.
# generated by run_plan_close2.sh S4
== GEMM_MODE=A /home/treo/.cache/b70cases/gg_q405_E512 rows=64 ks=2
gemm A (sequential bucket launches): rows 64 = NSLAB 4 x 16 rows/launch, RPAD 16, PART rows 64, threads 160 x 512 x NSLAB
case /home/treo/.cache/b70cases/gg_q405_E512: E 512 R 64 k 2560 n 640 K 4  trellis 400.00 MiB  KS 2  layout native
rev L: dpas 8 x 2 per byte-block (rows padded to 16), 1 expert/thread, 160 x 512 threads (2048 HW)
revL ks 2 rows 64 1-proj     layout native:   4662.2 us    179.9 G-w/s    90.0 GB/s(trellis)   [single-launch  4646.7 us]  [M 8x2, 40 tiles x 512 experts]

=== READOUT ==============================================================
K=4 (Qwen3.8@4.05, E=512, rows=64, ks=2): 4662.2 us for one projection = 9.11 us per expert-bucket.
Compare K=2 from out_probe_gemm_midE.txt: 7.14-7.25 us per bucket. Doubling the bytes per bucket costs
+28 pct, not +100 pct, so bucket cost is dominated by FIXED per-bucket overhead at these shapes:
   cost/bucket ~= 4.6 us + 1.13 us x K   (two points, K=2 and K=4; K=3 unmeasured in THIS instrument)
PROVISIONAL: two points fit a line, they do not establish one, and the K=3 value used elsewhere (5.70
us/bucket in D18) came from engine-integrated prefill, not this probe, so the three must not be averaged.
What it does say, if it holds: moving to a higher quant costs the card sub-proportionally in time, and
effective trellis bandwidth RISES with K (56-60 GB/s at K=2 vs 90 GB/s at K=4 on the same shape), because
bytes grow while the fixed bucket cost does not. The card is therefore relatively better at high quants --
which is where the parent degrades most (out_prefill_decomp.txt: 4.05 prefill is 77 pct copy traffic).
Missing rungs before this is a law: K=3 in this instrument, and K=6.
== GEMM_MODE=A /home/treo/.cache/b70cases/gg_q605_E512 rows=64 ks=2  (K=6 rung, added by hand after the queue)
gemm A (sequential bucket launches): rows 64 = NSLAB 4 x 16 rows/launch, RPAD 16, PART rows 64, threads 160 x 512 x NSLAB
case /home/treo/.cache/b70cases/gg_q605_E512: E 512 R 64 k 2560 n 640 K 6  trellis 600.00 MiB  KS 2  layout native
rev L: dpas 8 x 2 per byte-block (rows padded to 16), 1 expert/thread, 160 x 512 threads (2048 HW)
revL ks 2 rows 64 1-proj     layout native:   6117.7 us    137.1 G-w/s   102.8 GB/s(trellis)   [single-launch  6090.7 us]  [M 8x2, 40 tiles x 512 experts]

=== READOUT v2 (three rungs; supersedes the two-point provisional note above) =================
per expert-projection bucket, rows=64, ks=2, E=512 (E=256/128 for K=2 from out_probe_gemm_midE.txt):

    K   us/bucket   trellis MiB/expert-proj   GB/s(trellis)   cost vs K=2
    2      7.14-7.25            0.39              56-60          1.00
    4      9.11                 0.78                90           1.27
    6     11.95                 1.17               103           1.66

Least squares through the three: cost ~= 4.8 us + 1.19 us x K, and the K=4 point lands 5 % off that line, which is
close enough to accept "fixed + slope in K" and far enough to keep the residuals visible. The load-bearing number
is the intercept: about 4.8 us of every bucket is NOT bytes -- at K=2 that is 67 % of the cost. Implications:

  * D18 stands and sharpens: cost is per bucket, and most of a bucket is fixed overhead. Byte-rate models are
    wrong mainly at low K, where the fixed part dominates.
  * Tripling bytes (K=2 -> 6) costs 1.66x, so the card degrades sub-proportionally with quant while the parent
    degrades super-proportionally (4.05 prefill is already 77 % copy, GLM 81 %).
  * Effective trellis bandwidth rises 56 -> 103 GB/s across this range and is nowhere near the ~292 GB/s the copy
    peak allows, which is the quantitative statement of why rows-deep and SLM staging could not win: the kernel is
    leaving bandwidth on the table because per-bucket fixed cost, not DRAM, sets the pace.
  * Still missing before this is a law: K=3 in this instrument (5.70 us/bucket came from engine-integrated prefill
    and must not be blended with these probe numbers), and rows dependence (all three points are rows=64).
== GEMM_MODE=A /home/treo/.cache/b70cases/gg_q268_E512 rows=64 ks=2  (K=3 rung, closes the gap in the 4.8+1.19K fit)
missing meta.json

=== CORRECTION to the "K=3 missing" line in READOUT v2 =====================================
K=3 is not a missing rung of THIS family: Qwen3.8 exports are K=2 (2.05), K=2.5 (2.68 -- which is why the dumper
refuses it, the ring math needs integers), K=4 (4.05), K=5 (4.18/5.05), K=6 (6.05). So 2/4/6 is the whole reachable
integer ladder for Qwen, and the fit is not interpolated across a gap. The K=3 point that does exist belongs to
GLM, measured separately at a different expert size in out_probe_gemm_glm.txt -- and that comparison is what shows
there is no single fixed+slope*K law across geometries.
